The Galatia Training: The Definitive Guide to Molding Your Own Potential

The video explains how expectations shape performance, the effects of Pigmalion and Golem and the self-efficacy of Albert Bandura, and shows how the internal saboteur stops the realization. It proposes the Galatean Training, with four pillars: radical self-awareness, strategic effort, constructive internal dialogue and mastery engineering.

Do expectations create reality?

The video starts from an idea that comes from psychology and mythology: can expectations create reality? 00:00 This phenomenon influences performance in schools, offices and personal life 00:20.

Pigmalion and Golem

There are two opposing forces: the Pygmalion effect and the Golem effect 00:20. They show an almost direct connection between what is expected of someone and the result that the person delivers: high expectations tend to improve performance, and low expectations can sabotage the potential 00:41.

The name of the Golem effect comes from the legend of the clay creature that does not reach its potential. Low expectations, ours or the others, have seen a psychological barrier 01:03.

The two effects are examples of self-fulfilling prophecy: something that becomes real because it is believed to happen 01:25.

Self-efficacy

Everything is based on self-efficacy, the concept of the 1977 psychologist Albert Bandura. Self-efficacy is not having the skills, but believing that one has 01:25. This belief defines the effort, persistence and size of goals 01:46.

It is built from four sources 02:07:

1. The victories themselves, the experiments of mastery 02:07. 2. Seeing similar people succeed 02:07. 3. The encouragement, verbal persuasion of others 02:07. 4. The Emotional States 02:27.

The internal saboteur

As it is built, belief can be sabotaged, often by internal forces 02:27.

Psychologist W. R. D. Fairbairn named this conflict: the internal saboteur, a part of the mind that works against its own goals and is born of past frustrations 02:49. He hits head-on with the central ego, the conscious part he wants to accomplish. It is the voice filled with resentment that strikes precisely the quest for fulfillment 03:10.

In everyday life, it appears in mental traps 03:31:

  • The fallacy of planning: to think that a task takes an hour and she takes five 03:31.
  • The negative attribution: when it goes wrong, it is our fault; when it works, it was luck 03:51.
  • The endless search for external approval 03:51.

All these patterns feed the saboteur and undermine self-efficacy 03:51.

The Galatean Training

The answer is a practical method, the Galatean Training, so that each person is the sculptor himself 04:13. It has four pillars, which fight the saboteur and build self-efficacy 04:13:

1. Radical self-awareness 04:35. 2. Strategic effort 04:35. 3. Constructive internal dialogue 04:354. 4. Engineering of mastery 04:35.

Radical self-awareness

It is not enough "acho that I am good at it". The proposal is to look at the facts of history itself 04:55. The question: thinking of three great successes of the past, what talents led to these results consistently? 04:55 Focus comes out of what's missing and goes to what's proven to have worked 05:15.

Strategic effort

This pillar means effort and failure: all stumbling becomes information to grow 05:15. Failure doesn't say anything about someone's ability, but the strategy didn't work. 05:37. Instead of trying harder, seek a better strategy 05:37.

Constructive internal dialogue

The idea is to take control of internal conversation, as do high-performance athletes 05:58. Swap "I won't get" for a clear instruction, like " firm body, focus on the target", changes the game. It is to use in itself the verbal persuasion of Bandura 06:18.

Engineering of mastery

If self-efficacy comes from successful experiences, it is necessary to create them and actively build evidence that one is capable of 06:39. Consistent small wins are worth more than a big win once in a while. 06:59:

1. Break big goals in tiny steps 06:59. 2. Run every step and recognize it as success 06:59. 3. Use the energy of this victory for the next step in a snowball effect 07:19.

Sculptor and work

The goal is to stop relying on external validation and rely on your own ability 07:19. True trust is never to fail, it is to believe that effort is worth it 07:40.

Galatea, in mythology, is the statue that hopes to be carved. The proposal is to be both the sculptor and the work 07:40. The final reflection: if beliefs are the chisel that shapes the stone, what work is each sculpting? 08:03

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the difference between the Pygmalion effect and the Golem effect?

Pigmalion shows that high expectations improve performance. Golem shows that low expectations sabotage him 00:41.

What is self-efficacy?

According to Albert Bandura, it is the belief that you have the skills to accomplish something. It defines the effort, persistence and size of goals 01:25.

About the video

Have you ever wondered if your expectations can actually create your reality?

In this deep video, we dive into the pillars of psychology to unravel the secret of Self-fulfilling Prophecy and how it dictates its success. Discover the two powerful forces that influence your performance—the Pigmalion Effect (high expectations) and the Golem Effect (low expectations)—and how they manifest themselves in your life.

The key lies in your Self-efficacy (the central concept of Albert Bandura): the belief that you have the skills to accomplish something.

We present the GALATEY TRAINING, a practical four-pillar method to help you become your own sculptor, build an unwavering confidence and silence that inner voice that sabotages you.

In this Video, you will learn:
[00:34] The Two Forces: Understand the dynamics between the Pigmalian Effect and the Golem Effect.

[01:42] Self effectiveness: What is and how this fundamental belief dictates the size of the goals you propose.

[02:48] The internal saboteur: Like internal conflict (a "critical voice" Fairbairn) paralyzes its realization.

[03:41] Mental Traps: Identify common patterns that undermine your self-efficacy (failure of planning, negative assignment, and search for external approval).

The 4 Pillars of the Galatean Training:
[04:39] Radical self-consciousness: The technique to identify your proven core talents instead of focusing on what's missing.

[05:36] Strategic Effort: Resigning failure as information and focusing on stronger strategies.

[06:08] Construction Internal Dialogue: Take control of your internal narrative, using verbal persuasion in yourself.

[06:46] Mastery Engineering: The method of consistent small wins to actively build proof that you are capable (the "Snowball effect" of trust).

True trust is not about never failing, it's about believing that effort is worth it.

The Final Reflection: Stop being the statue, hoping to be carved. Become the sculptor and masterpiece.
